item.title: zizonline.com: 70. The gap: HSTS.
item.description:
Every internal link that was opened answered, and AI answer and search crawlers may read the start page. But HSTS is not sent.
The lesson for every team: Send Strict-Transport-Security with a max-age of at least a year, so browsers never try plain http again.
One automated analysis of public pages on 26 Oct 2026, one of the most visited sites in its country, from QA-lab URL Review's country sweep. A starting point, not a verdict. item.description:

item.description:

The lesson for every team: Give every page a canonical link, even when only one address serves it. One line settles which URL ranks.

item.title: Valle del Cauca locks the pinch-zoom.
item.description:
HSTS runs a full year, framing is limited, and cookies are Secure. But the viewport tag says user-scalable=no, so people who need larger text cannot pinch to zoom on a phone.
The lesson for every team: Drop user-scalable=no and maximum-scale from the viewport tag, so people can zoom to at least 200%.
One automated analysis of public pages on 21 Oct 2026. A starting point, not a verdict. How the review works, step by step: https://carlosandmunoz.com/qa-review-guide.html?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=runs-3-2027-01&utm_content=valle

item.description:

item.title: Policía Nacional's search has no label.
item.description:
HSTS with preload, framing limited to its own origin, a declared language, and every internal link opened answered. But the home page search box and volume slider have no label, so screen readers announce blank fields.
The lesson for every team: Tie each field to a <label for>, or give it an aria-label. A screen reader can only announce a name that exists.

item.description:

Try this today: Pick the one action each key page exists for. Make sure an event fires only when it succeeds.
